title: Why Does Bravo Have 2 Different Interfaces?
blurb: A deeper look at Tap and Scan

slides.title: Why does Bravo have 2 different interfaces?
slides.text: Why does Bravo have 2 different interfaces? A deeper look at Tap and Scan

slides.title: The starting point
slides.text: The starting point One interface can’t serve every user Other AAC apps interface, usually designed for direct-select users Bravo interfaces, each built for how its user communicates

slides.title: Two design goals
slides.text: Two design goals Flexibility and efficiency Tap · ultimate flexibility Scan · ultimate efficiency

slides.title: Tap vs. Scan · Selecting
slides.text: Tap vs. Scan · Selecting How an option gets chosen  Tap The user taps an option on the screen.  Scan The user usually presses a switch. Tapping the screen works too.

slides.title: Tap vs. Scan · Selecting
slides.text: Tap vs. Scan · Selecting The auditory scanning loop 1 · Highlight Option is read to the user, usually on a personal speaker 2 · Decide Does the user press the switch? 3 · Announce Spoken aloud on the system speaker Next option Bravo moves on and highlights it Yes No

slides.title: Tap vs. Scan · Building a message
slides.text: Tap vs. Scan · Building a message Building blocks or whole phrases Tap: building blocks I want go park Choose individual words or small phrases Scan: phrases I want to go to the park Select a more developed phrase in one choice

slides.title: Tap vs. Scan · The grid
slides.text: Tap vs. Scan · The grid Flexible grid, basic grid Tap: choose exactly how many options to show. Enough to choose from, never overwhelming. Scan: a simple grid. The count matters less, because options are scanned.

slides.title: Tap vs. Scan · Images
slides.text: Tap vs. Scan · Images Pictures on, pictures off Tap Images by default Turn them off for users who can read the options. Scan Text by default Turn images on for users who like to watch the screen.

slides.title:  In both interfaces
slides.text:  In both interfaces Wake Word works everywhere A partner asks a question, and Bravo generates options to respond.

slides.title: Summary
slides.text: Summary Tap and Scan at a glance Tap Scan Designed for Ultimate flexibility Ultimate efficiency Selecting Tap the screen Switch, or tap the screen Strategy Building blocks: words, small phrases Developed phrases Grid Flexible: exact number of options Basic: count matters less Images On by default, can turn off Off by default, can turn on Wake Word Yes

title: How Does Bravo Use AI?
blurb: And what makes it different from other AAC apps that use AI

slides.title: How does Bravo use AI?
slides.text: How does Bravo use AI? And what makes it different from other AAC apps that use AI

slides.title: AI and AAC
slides.text: AI and AAC A very natural partnership LLM Large Language Model When people say “AI” today, they mostly mean Large Language Models, or LLMs.

slides.title: AI and AAC
slides.text: AI and AAC How an LLM works Identify natural patterns in language Understand how those patterns work Predict the next likely option AAC does exactly the same: analyze the pattern, then predict the next option.

slides.title: AI and AAC
slides.text: AI and AAC Two jobs AI can do  Generate options for the user to select and communicate  Build the boards creating pages and filling them with options

slides.title: AI and AAC
slides.text: AI and AAC Building a Greetings board Before AI 1 Search the web for “10 common greetings” 2 Create a new page called Greetings 3 Add the options, one at a time With AI 1 Tell Bravo the board’s purpose: “Greetings” AI finds the options, builds the board and adds them for you.

slides.title: What makes Bravo different
slides.text: What makes Bravo different Four unique AI features Layers of context in every AI prompt AI prompts in buttons not just in page building Next options generated after every selection Wake Word turns a partner’s words into a prompt

slides.title: Feature 1 · Context
slides.text: Feature 1 · Context What is context? Context gives the AI prompt more information, so it can generate more nuanced options. Greetings Happy Greetings Christmas Greetings

slides.title: Feature 1 · Context
slides.text: Feature 1 · Context Multiple layers of context Right now Mood Location People nearby Activity Date Time About the user Favorite topics Least favorite topics Recent activities Upcoming activities Any of these can shape how and what we communicate.

slides.title: Feature 1 · Context
slides.text: Feature 1 · Context Same moment, different mood Mood: happy “Good morning!” Mood: tired “Not ready for today”

slides.title: Feature 1 · Context
slides.text: Feature 1 · Context Where context comes from  The Admin enters most of the context  The user picks their mood when the app starts  Bravo can improve it over time from what the user selects, if enabled

slides.title:  Completely optional. Never shared.
slides.text:  Completely optional. Never shared. Every layer of context is optional, and Bravo still generates dynamic options without any of it.

slides.title: Feature 2 · AI prompts in buttons
slides.text: Feature 2 · AI prompts in buttons A button can hold an AI prompt Example prompts on the Scan interface “Generate greetings based on current location” “Generate ways to describe something positive” “Generate jokes”

slides.title: Feature 2 · AI prompts in buttons
slides.text: Feature 2 · AI prompts in buttons What happens when it’s selected User selects the button Prompt plus any context goes to the AI AI generates options and builds the page Bravo opens the new page

slides.title: Feature 2 · AI prompts in buttons
slides.text: Feature 2 · AI prompts in buttons greetings pages for 10 moods button that builds the page for today’s mood

slides.title: Feature 3 · Next options · Scan
slides.text: Feature 3 · Next options · Scan Scan: phrases that keep it going User selects I want to go outside Bravo can offer Do you want to go outside too? A full set of phrases to continue the message and engage the partner.

slides.title: Feature 3 · Next options · Tap
slides.text: Feature 3 · Next options · Tap Tap: the next building blocks want to go outside New options appear in the Dynamic row, outlined in purple.

slides.title: Feature 4 · Wake Word
slides.text: Feature 4 · Wake Word AAC’s big challenge: responding When a partner asks a question in traditional AAC:  Not programmed A good answer may simply not exist on any board  Yes or no The question gets boiled down to a simple yes or no  Too slow The answer exists, but takes time to find

slides.title: Feature 4 · Wake Word
slides.text: Feature 4 · Wake Word Bravo generates the answers  Partner says the Wake Word, then asks or comments  Their words become an AI prompt  Response options appear, ready to choose The status message shows Bravo is listening

slides.title: Recap
slides.text: Recap How Bravo’s AI is different Feature What it does 1 · Layers of context Mood, location, people, topics and more shape every option 2 · Prompts in buttons One button builds a fresh page, on demand 3 · Next options New phrases or building blocks after each selection 4 · Wake Word A partner’s question becomes response options All context is optional, and never shared.

title: How Do I Use the Wake Word to Ask a Question?
blurb: Five steps, on both Scan and Tap

slides.title: How do I use the Wake Word to ask a question?
slides.text: How do I use the Wake Word to ask a question? Five steps, on both Scan and Tap

slides.title: The Wake Word
slides.text: The Wake Word A new way to start a conversation  More interaction Partners can ask a question or share a comment, and the user can answer right away.  Works like a smart assistant If you’ve said “Alexa” or “Hey Siri”, you already know how it works.

slides.title: The process
slides.text: The process Five steps from question to answer Partner Says the Wake Word Bravo Says “I’m listening” Asks a question or comments Generates response options User Selects, and gets follow-ups

slides.title: Before you start
slides.text: Before you start Choosing the Wake Word Set by the Admin at setup, and can be changed later The default is “Hey Bravo” Usually “Hey” + the user’s name: “Hey Bobby”

slides.title: Step 1 of 5
slides.text: Step 1 of 5 Say the Wake Word Scan Tap Always listening, even while scanning Auditory scanning: the mic is in the personal speaker

slides.title: Step 2 of 5
slides.text: Step 2 of 5 Wait for “I’m listening” Scan Tap Bravo says “I’m listening” out loud and shows it on screen. Then it’s your turn.

slides.title: Step 3 of 5
slides.text: Step 3 of 5 Ask a question or share a comment Speak after “I’m listening” Short or long questions both work Bravo stops listening after a pause  2 seconds of silence ends the question

slides.title: Step 3 of 5 · Tip
slides.text: Step 3 of 5 · Tip Include context in your question  “What do you think about the Broncos big win yesterday?”  “What do you want to eat from McDonald’s?” The more detail in the question, the more specific the answers Bravo can offer.

slides.title: Step 3 of 5
slides.text: Step 3 of 5 Bravo confirms what it heard Scan Tap Shows “Hearing: …” , then says “Give me a moment to respond”

slides.title: Step 4 of 5
slides.text: Step 4 of 5 Bravo generates ways to respond Scan Tap Scan: full phrases to answer Tap: building blocks to answer Shaped by context: mood, favorites and more

slides.title: Step 5 of 5
slides.text: Step 5 of 5 Select an answer, and keep talking Scan Tap The answer is spoken aloud, and follow-up options keep coming until another board is chosen

slides.title: Not the right words?
slides.text: Not the right words? Four ways to find more options  More Options Generates a new set  Something Else  Another board Go to any board you like  Free Style Even more words and phrases

slides.title: Troubleshooting
slides.text: Troubleshooting If the Wake Word doesn’t respond  Try another spelling Set the name as “John” instead of “Jon”  Wait for it to finish Listening may pause while the app works, like loading a page  Say it again Repeat the Wake Word if it was paused or misheard

slides.title: Recap
slides.text: Recap The Wake Word in five steps Step What happens What you’ll see or hear Say the Wake Word “Hey Bobby” Bravo confirms “I’m listening” Ask, with context “Hearing: …” then “Give me a moment to respond” Bravo offers answers Phrases (Scan) or building blocks (Tap) Select and keep talking Answer spoken, follow-ups appear
